caption: Integers pass through unchanged
Threads element-wise over a list
sage.note: compute-engine's Floor is Listable and threads over the list; Sage's takes scalars only.
sympy.note: compute-engine's Floor threads over (or pools) the list; SymPy's takes scalars.
mpmath.note: compute-engine's Floor threads over the list; mpmath's takes scalars.
rust.note: compute-engine's Floor is Listable and threads over the list; the Rust crates take scalars.

caption: A free variable added to an integer is still untouched
Stays symbolic
Exact radicals are decided numerically
Floor(Sqrt(-1)) stays complex: Floor is a no-op on a non-real value
sage.note: compute-engine's Floor is a no-op on the already-integral complex value i; Sage's floor() declines outright on an element of a complex quadratic number field.
rust.note: Rust's f64 sqrt is real-only and gives NaN; compute-engine's Floor is a no-op on the resulting complex value.

caption: Evaluates at an exact constant: $\lfloor\pi\rfloor = 3$
...and at its negative, $\lfloor -\pi \rfloor = -4$
A second argument floors to a multiple of it -- the nearest multiple of 10 below 226
...the step needn't be an integer: $3.5 \cdot \lfloor -10.3/3.5 \rfloor = -10.5$
...nor rational: $2\pi - e \approx 3.57$ floors to the multiple $5/2$ of $5/4$
Floors the real and imaginary parts separately
sage.note: compute-engine evaluates Floor on a complex float, flooring the real and imaginary parts separately; Sage's floor() leaves the complex argument unevaluated, printing it back symbolically.

caption: How many full 5-item packs fit in 17 items
Legendre's formula: $100!$ ends in $\lfloor 100/5 \rfloor + \lfloor 100/25 \rfloor = 24$ zeros
The number of decimal digits of n is $\lfloor \log_{10} n \rfloor + 1$
The first four digits of $e$
For a non-integer x, $\lceil x \rceil = \lfloor x \rfloor + 1$. See [[Ceil]]
$\lfloor -x \rfloor = -\lceil x \rceil$
Idempotent: $\lfloor\lfloor x \rfloor\rfloor = \lfloor x \rfloor$, since the inner value is already an integer
A division by zero inside Floor simplifies to ComplexInfinity
sage.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers Floor(ComplexInfinity), and Sage's exact rational division raises a ZeroDivisionError before Floor is even applied.
rust.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers "ComplexInfinity", and Rust's exact division panics on the zero denominator before Floor is even applied.
